summary: TensorRT INT8 engine build failed for the YOLO26n end-to-end ONNX graph. The error occurs during calibration graph optimization, not during calibration data feeding or inference. This is a TensorRT 10.3.0 internal assertion failure triggered by the end-to-end NMS topology (TopK/GatherElements/Gather ops) in the YOLO26n ONNX graph.

attempts.error: Error[2]: [checkSanity.cpp::checkLinks::218] Error Code 2: Internal Error (Assertion item.second != nullptr failed. region should have been removed from Graph::regions)
attempts.log_excerpt: Perform graph optimization on calibration graph. → Error[2]: checkSanity.cpp::checkLinks:218 assertion failed

attempts.method: Python API: IInt8EntropyCalibrator2 with 200 COCO val2017 calibration images
attempts.error: Same checkSanity.cpp::checkLinks assertion error during build_serialized_network()
attempts.note: Calibrator get_batch() was never called — the build fails before calibration data is needed, proving the error is in the graph optimization phase, not the calibration data

attempts.method: Python API: IInt8EntropyCalibrator2 + CALIBRATE_BEFORE_FUSION quantization flag
attempts.note: CALIBRATE_BEFORE_FUSION flag (calibrate before graph fusion) did not work around the bug
Lowering optimization level to 0 (no graph optimization) did not help — the calibration graph itself fails

attempts.result: BUILD_SUCCEEDED but no actual INT8 quantization
attempts.note: The --stronglyTyped flag bypasses the checkLinks bug but creates a strongly-typed network that only uses INT8 where the ONNX has explicit Q/DQ (QuantizeDequantize) nodes. Since the YOLO26n ONNX has no Q/DQ nodes, this engine has all-FP32 I/O (DataType.FLOAT) and no actual INT8 layers. It is effectively an FP32 engine with INT8 flag. Layer count: 342. This is a valid engine but it is NOT an INT8 quantized model.

Without a calibration cache, trtexec creates a default IInt8EntropyCalibrator2 but has no calibration data to feed. The process hangs indefinitely (killed after 5+ minutes). This is expected behavior — trtexec --int8 without --calib requires calibration data from a prior run.

root_cause_analysis.error: checkSanity.cpp::checkLinks:218 — Assertion item.second != nullptr failed. region should have been removed from Graph::regions
root_cause_analysis.trigger: The YOLO26n end-to-end ONNX graph contains a TopK + GatherElements + Gather pattern (from the baked-in NMS in model.23 head). During INT8 calibration graph optimization, TensorRT 10.3.0 attempts to optimize this pattern and hits an internal assertion failure in the region/link tracking.
root_cause_analysis.why_fp32_fp16_work: The FP32 and FP16 engines (from attempt45) build successfully because they don't use the INT8 calibration graph path — they use the standard graph optimization which handles the TopK/Gather pattern correctly.
root_cause_analysis.why_stronglytyped_works_but_useless: The --stronglyTyped path uses explicit quantization (Q/DQ nodes) instead of implicit calibration. Since it never enters the calibration graph optimization path, it avoids the bug. But without Q/DQ nodes in the ONNX, no layer is actually quantized to INT8.
potential_workarounds_not_attempted: Export the YOLO26n model with explicit Q/DQ nodes (ONNX QuantizeDequantize ops) and use --stronglyTyped. This would require PyTorch quantization-aware training (QAT) or post-training quantization export, which is out of scope.

Export the YOLO26n model as a raw-output (non-e2e) ONNX without baked-in NMS. The TopK/GatherElements/Gather ops would be removed from the graph, allowing INT8 calibration of the Conv/MatMul layers. This requires modifying the model export and implementing NMS in post-processing.
Upgrade TensorRT to a version that fixes the checkLinks assertion. At the time of this test, TensorRT 10.3.0 is the latest available on Jetson Orin Nano.

gates.note: Parity gates not applicable — INT8 engine could not be built. Status is FAIL (build failure), not FAIL (parity failure).

fp32_fp16_reference.note: FP32 and FP16 engines build and pass parity (from attempt45 evidence). Only INT8 fails to build.

non_claims: Not a certification or signed result.
Not a claim that TensorRT INT8 cannot work for YOLO26n; only that it fails to build on TensorRT 10.3.0 with this end-to-end ONNX graph.
The failure is a TensorRT internal assertion in the INT8 calibration graph optimization, triggered by the TopK/GatherElements/Gather NMS pattern.
A raw-output (non-e2e) ONNX graph or an ONNX with explicit Q/DQ nodes would likely avoid this bug but was not tested.
TensorRT INT8 calibration was attempted with 200 representative COCO val2017 images (available on Jetson) and the IInt8EntropyCalibrator2.
OpenVINO INT8 (separate target) was also tested extensively — see docs/evidence/yolo26n-openvino-int8-apple-cpu-FAIL.json.
Axelera Metis AIPU INT8 (separate target) was also tested — see docs/evidence/yolo26n-axelera-metis-aipu-int8-FAIL.json.
